title: Music and singing — music vocals
explanation: Music never appears in training. Here it is largely suppressed (-18.5 dB on average), but the gain jumps by 12.2 dB from frame to frame as sung or tonal passages are mistaken for voiced speech, so what remains warbles in level.
source_note: MUSAN music-fma-0063 (singing), 10 s excerpt; no clean reference - the model should pass or suppress it consistently, singing tends to be partly kept as speech

title: Music and singing — music instrumental
explanation: Music never appears in training. Here it is largely suppressed (-24.8 dB on average), but the gain jumps by 8.8 dB from frame to frame as sung or tonal passages are mistaken for voiced speech, so what remains warbles in level.
source_note: MUSAN music-jamendo-0005 (instrumental), 10 s excerpt; tonal music is not in the training noise, expect partial suppression and warbling

title: Music and singing — music speech bg
explanation: Music under speech is reduced by 11.2 dB (VB-D test average: 13.1 dB); its harmonics look like voiced speech to the model, so it partly survives (PESQ 1.08 → 1.72).
source_note: VB-D p257_256 over MUSAN music-jamendo-0005 (instrumental) at 5 dB SNR

title: Long pause with residual noise — silence 1
explanation: In the 5.7 s pause the background is turned down by only 13.8 dB (to -62.2 dBFS): the model leaves a noise floor instead of gating pauses to silence. The residual keeps the input's texture (6.8 vs 6.4 dB frame-to-frame spread), so there is no audible pumping.
source_note: VB-D p257_182 (2.3 s), 5.7 s pause, p257_203 (2.0 s); VB-D 'living room' noise at 25 dB SNR throughout - watch for noise pumping in the pause

title: Long pause with residual noise — silence 2
explanation: In the 6.0 s pause the background is turned down by only 16.7 dB (to -59.3 dBFS): the model leaves a noise floor instead of gating pauses to silence. The residual keeps the input's texture (5.3 vs 6.4 dB frame-to-frame spread), so there is no audible pumping.
source_note: VB-D p232_080 (2.1 s), 6.0 s pause, p257_034 (1.9 s); VB-D 'office' noise at 20 dB SNR throughout - watch for noise pumping in the pause

title: Very low SNR — low snr bus m5db
explanation: The model removes 20.1 dB of noise and SI-SDR rises from -6.2 to 11.3 dB, but the speech is moderately distorted (speech-only SI-SDR 15.6 dB) and quality stays low (PESQ 1.14 → 2.17, STOI 0.76 → 0.89): at this SNR the mask cannot separate speech from noise reliably.
source_note: VB-D p257_347 with its own 'bus' noise rescaled from 2.5 dB to -5 dB SNR

title: Very low SNR — low snr cafe m10db
explanation: The model removes 19.9 dB of noise and SI-SDR rises from -10.9 to 2.1 dB, but the speech itself is badly damaged (speech-only SI-SDR 5.8 dB) and quality stays low (PESQ 1.06 → 1.22, STOI 0.72 → 0.72): at this SNR the mask cannot separate speech from noise reliably.
source_note: VB-D p232_009 with its own 'cafe' noise rescaled from 7.5 dB to -10 dB SNR

title: Very low SNR — low snr public square m10db
explanation: The model removes 25.9 dB of noise and SI-SDR rises from -11.2 to 10.5 dB, but the speech is moderately distorted (speech-only SI-SDR 13.0 dB) and quality stays low (PESQ 1.06 → 1.70, STOI 0.72 → 0.80): at this SNR the mask cannot separate speech from noise reliably.
source_note: VB-D p257_402 with its own 'public square' noise rescaled from 7.5 dB to -10 dB SNR

title: Competing talker — talker 1
explanation: The interfering voice is attenuated by just 3.3 dB: the model is trained to keep all speech and has no notion of which talker is the target. PESQ stays at 1.35.
source_note: VB-D p232_058 + LibriSpeech speaker 8555 (other gender) at 0 dB SIR - the model was never trained to remove speech, so the interferer is expected to stay

title: Competing talker — talker 2
explanation: The interfering voice is attenuated by just 1.6 dB: the model is trained to keep all speech and has no notion of which talker is the target. PESQ stays at 1.13.
source_note: VB-D p232_117 + LibriSpeech speaker 7127 (same gender) at 0 dB SIR - the model was never trained to remove speech, so the interferer is expected to stay

title: Heavy reverberation — reverb 1
explanation: The reverberant tail is reduced by only 2.7 dB relative to the direct path: this tail is longer than most training rooms (T60 up to 0.8 s), and the model only learns to remove late reverberation, keeping the first 50 ms of reflections.
source_note: VB-D p257_411 convolved with sim_te_00253 (simulated, T60 0.90 s, DRR 2.3 dB); clean = time-aligned direct path. Heavy reverb is outside the benchmark model's training data (reverb augmentation is demo-only)

title: Heavy reverberation — reverb 2
explanation: The reverberant tail is reduced by only 3.0 dB relative to the direct path: this tail is longer than most training rooms (T60 up to 0.8 s), and the model only learns to remove late reverberation, keeping the first 50 ms of reflections.
source_note: VB-D p232_013 convolved with sim_te_00160 (simulated, T60 0.89 s, DRR -4.9 dB); clean = time-aligned direct path. Heavy reverb is outside the benchmark model's training data (reverb augmentation is demo-only)

title: Clipped input — clipping 1
explanation: Clipping distortion (3% of samples at full scale) is correlated with the speech, so it is kept: the error against the unclipped reference (noise plus distortion) drops by only -0.5 dB and PESQ goes 2.23 → 3.21, although the background noise itself is removed.
source_note: VB-D p232_227 noisy (office, 12.5 dB) +14.9 dB then hard-clipped (3% of samples clipped); clean is the unclipped reference at its original level

title: Clipped input — clipping 2
explanation: Clipping distortion (15% of samples at full scale) is correlated with the speech, so it is kept: the error against the unclipped reference (noise plus distortion) drops by only -0.4 dB and PESQ goes 1.61 → 2.11, although the background noise itself is removed.
source_note: VB-D p232_148 noisy (bus, 12.5 dB) +21.3 dB then hard-clipped (15% of samples clipped); clean is the unclipped reference at its original level
